content.thinking:
My C++ capture produced an image that pyref rejects with "empty base": a node whose pattern is 0 (no NI entries) has ni_base != 0.

In my builder, for a node with pattern 0, `n->ni_base = img.nexthops.size()` — which is nonzero if previous nodes already appended entries! The protocol says "Empty arrays have base0". So I must set ni_base = 0 when the NI list is empty.

Let me fix the builder: `n->ni_base = n->ni.empty() ? 0 : img.nexthops.size();`

Also check my C++ validator handles this ✓ (it requires base==0 for k==0 ✓).

Good, the cross-testing is already useful.

Let me also review other places... In the builder, nodes with pattern 0 → bitmap_id points to pattern 0 ✓ and the zero pattern is added to pattern_set ✓.

Fix and rebuild.

arguments.command:
cd /workspace/src && python3 - <<'PY'
p='mem_init.cpp'
s=open(p).read()
old="""        n->bitmap_id = pattern_id[n->pattern];
        n->ni_base = static_cast<uint32_t>(img.nexthops.size());"""
new="""        n->bitmap_id = pattern_id[n->pattern];
        n->ni_base = n->ni.empty() ? 0u : static_cast<uint32_t>(img.nexthops.size());  // empty arrays use base0"""
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
